maintainer: Google DeepMind
measures: 400 multiple-choice visual questions on spatial, trajectory, action, state-estimation, pointing, multi-view and task reasoning; scored as accuracy.

caveat: CONFIRMED on the primary page: the 2026-10-13 Google Developers Blog post 'Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics' does name ERQA and states 87% ('Using pure reasoning'). The Haiku file wrongly said ERQA was not named in the text. The post gives the number only in prose; the comparison chart is an image (gemini-4-argon__benchmark__robotics.jpg), so the other models' scores are not in the text. Vendor-reported, benchmark owned by the same vendor. No official leaderboard in the GitHub repo (README ships a Gemini/OpenAI eval harness only). 'Pure reasoning' presumably means no tool use/thinking-only; the post does not define it. Introduced in the Gemini Robotics tech report (arXiv 2503.20020, March 2025); the arXiv HTML spells the count '400' (rendered '400400' once MathML is stripped).

quote_leader: You can see this leap in capability on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark, which tests a model's ability to understand and solve physical, spatial problems in 3D environments. Using pure reasoning, Argon scores 87%, outperforming every other frontier model.

caveat: Numbers read directly from the live JSON API the site calls (https://roboarena-api-domain-name.online/api/leaderboard, last_updated 2026-10-27T02:09:55Z, i.e. the evening of 2026-10-26 US time). 24 policies listed. The top two have wide uncertainty bands (j2-vla std 106 on only 25 evals; DreamZero std 42.6 on 190), so rank 1 vs 2 is not statistically separated; pi05_droid/pi0_fast_droid are the highly sampled baselines (745/941 evals). Others on board: AllenAI MolmoAct2-DROID 1579, G0.5-Droid-AR 1559, Cosmos3-Nano-Policy 1299 (only 2 evals, std 347; NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 Nano). Site's JS maps ids to display names (dreaming_zebra->DreamZero, j2-vla->Spirit v1.6). Developer/country of 'Spirit v1.6' is inferred, not stated. Scores are not comparable to fixed-task success rates.

Importantly, evaluators can freely choose the tasks and environments they evaluate on, enabling easy scaling of diversity, but they are required to perform double-blind evaluations over pairs of policies.

maintainer: Xueyang Zhou et al., Huazhong University of Science and Technology (with Harvard, MIT, Wuhan Univ. of Technology, Lehigh)
maintainer_country: China (lead institution HUST; mixed US co-authors)
measures: LIBERO extended with perturbations along four dimensions (manipulated objects, initial states, task instructions, environments) to separate generalization from memorization; success rate.
caveat: No leaderboard; this is a stress test of three models (OpenVLA, pi0, pi0.5) plus UniVLA in the README. The abstract's 'collapses to 0.0%' is NOT universal: in the README table all four models score 0.0 under P1 (task perturbation) but pi0.5 keeps 0.4 / 0.2 / 0.1 / 0.2 (Goal/Spatial/10/Object) under P2 (position perturbation), UniVLA 0.1 on Goal/Spatial. Units in the README are shown as 0-1 fractions (original 0.97), so 0.4 likely means 40%, but the unit is not stated. The 'above 90%' original-LIBERO figure is also not universal: pi0 on LIBERO-10 is 0.82 and UniVLA 0.61 on LIBERO-10. Authors' own result, not independently replicated.
quote_measures: we introduce LIBERO-PRO, an extended LIBERO benchmark that systematically evaluates model performance under reasonable perturbations across four dimensions: manipulated objects, initial states, task instructions, and environments.
quote_leader: although existing models achieve over 90% accuracy under the standard LIBERO evaluation, their performance collapses to 0.0% under our generalized setting.

maintainer: Senyu Fei et al. (author list includes Xipeng Qiu; GitHub sylvestf/LIBERO-plus)
maintainer_country: China (probable: Fudan-affiliated authors; affiliation line not fetched)
measures: Robustness of VLA models on LIBERO under controlled perturbations across seven dimensions: objects layout, camera viewpoints, robot initial states, language instructions, light conditions, background textures and sensor noise.
metric: success rate (%) per perturbation dimension and Total

leaders.model: OpenVLA-OFT+ (authors' own mix-SFT on LIBERO-plus data)

leaders.value: Avg 82.1 (README 'Research Works Using LIBERO-Plus', self-reported by the submitters)

caveat: The Haiku file's '79.6% OpenVLA-OFT' is wrong in attribution: 79.6 is the authors' own post-trained 'OpenVLA-OFT+' Total; plain OpenVLA-OFT is 69.6 Total (and 79.6 appears coincidentally as pi0's Light-column value in Table 1). Headline '95% to below 30%' is the abstract's wording: in Table 1 OpenVLA-OFT drops from 97.1 original to 59.7 (camera) and 37.2 (robot init), pi0 from 94.2 to 15.8 (camera) and 6.6 (robot init); OpenVLA falls from 76.5 to 1.1 (camera) and 4.1 (robot). So 'below 30%' holds for some model-dimension pairs, not all. README also carries SRPO 82.1 and AVA-VLA 74.7 and MergeVLA 72.2 averages as community-submitted. Language perturbations barely matter: the authors say models tend to ignore language instructions.
quote_measures: We perform a systematic vulnerability analysis by introducing controlled perturbations across seven dimensions: objects layout, camera viewpoints, robot initial states, language instructions, light conditions, background textures and sensor noise.
quote_leader: models exhibit extreme sensitivity to perturbation factors, including camera viewpoints and robot initial states, with performance dropping from 95% to below 30% under modest perturbations.

benchmark: SimplerEnv and validity audit 'What Are We Actually Benchmarking in Robot Manipulation?'
maintainer: SimplerEnv: Xuanlin Li, Hao Su, Ted Xiao et al. (UCSD/Google/Stanford/Berkeley; CoRL 2024); audit: Tianchong Jiang et al., Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago, Argonne, UChicago
measures: SimplerEnv: simulated real-to-sim evaluation of manipulation policies on Google Robot and WidowX+Bridge setups, validated by sim-vs-real correlation. Audit (arXiv 2606.04233, 2026-06): four diagnostics (shortcut solvability, statistical significance, creeping overfitting, data-source dependence) applied to LIBERO, CALVIN, SimplerEnv, RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0.
metric: success rate; audit reports share of SOTA claims that are provably significant
caveat: No SimplerEnv leaderboard exists; there is no single 'leader'. The audit statistic is exact: 19.8% (LIBERO) and 19.7% (SimplerEnv) of SOTA claims are provably significant; for RoboCasa and RoboTwin 2.0 the shares are 53.3% and 73.7%. This is a claim-level statistic about published SOTA claims, not a success rate. Other audit results: a 0.09B probe with no language encoder scores at or near reported SOTA on LIBERO; on CALVIN, resampling block poses within the training range lowers average tasks completed (of 5) from 4.17 to 3.14. The SimplerEnv-specific finding beyond the 19.7%: the authors modified the WidowX stack task (reversed instruction, support block) to test CogACT-Base, InternVLA-M1, X-VLA-WidowX and Dexbotic/DB-MemVLA. Haiku file said SimplerEnv finding was not extracted; it now is.
quote_measures: We audit LIBERO, CALVIN, SimplerEnv, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin 2.0 under these diagnostics.
quote_leader: On LIBERO and SimplerEnv, only 19.8% and 19.7% of SOTA claims, respectively, are provably significant.

maintainer: X Square Robot (X Square robot team plus outside collaborators); first author Lian Ruan
measures: Evolvable simulation benchmark on NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena for faithfully evaluating real-world performance of manipulation policies: 44 hierarchical long-horizon tasks across 10 capability dimensions, rule-based DAG subtask scoring (success rate and progress score), domain randomization and disjoint train/eval pipelines.
embodiments: ArtiXon Arm-6A dual-arm (self-developed), Franka (Robotiq/Panda hand), others
metric: success rate (%) and progress score (0-100), hierarchically macro-averaged

leaders.value: 53.9% ID overall success (67.3 progress) falling to 34.3% OOD (56.6 progress)

caveat: The 0.84 is NOT a success-rate correlation: the paper reports 0.74 linear correlation for success rate and 0.84 for progress score across all tasks (0.96 / 0.99 on general-manipulation tasks only), measured for one policy (Wall-OSS-0.5) trained on real data only. The abstract's wording 'a 0.84 linear correlation between simulated and real-robot evaluation results' glosses this. Four policies were evaluated (wall-oss-preview, Wall-OSS-0.5, DreamZero, pi0.5), all post-trained by the authors on the same demos from the ArtiXon Arm-6A; the best-performing policy is the authors' own internal model, so the ranking is vendor-run and vendor-favoring. A further 'Astra' model reaches 36.15% OOD success vs 34.3% for wall-oss-preview. The 2026-10-19 announcement and a public leaderboard for X2Real were not located; the '44 tasks' figure checks out against the arXiv abstract.
quote_measures: It features a comprehensive taxonomy with 10 capability dimensions and 44 hierarchical long-horizon tasks, covering basic manipulation skills and advanced capacities such as visual grounding, language understanding, and bimanual control.
quote_leader: Taking all tasks into account, our simulation environment achieves 0.74 linear correlation coefficient in success rate and 0.84 in progress score.

Scores are page-rendered values read 2026-10-26 from robocurve.org (homepage), with a release-date chart showing frontier mean score rising from 9.5% (2026-04-17) to 59.3% (2026-10-19). Different harness settings (medium/high effort, fast/priority tiers) are separate rows. The mean-score cell is over 120 attempts per configuration, so single-digit differences are not significant. Sibling 'Robot Capabilities Index' (2026-10-15 preprint page, 5 tasks, 9 models) finds RCI correlates r=0.85 with Blueprint-Bench 2 and that Gemini models outperform their general ECI (removing Gemini lifts ECI-RCI correlation from 0.20 to 0.96).

maintainer: Robocurve PBC (authors Edward Sun, Sravanthi Machcha, Sabrina Zou, Tzu Kit Chan, Jay Chooi)
measures: Whether frontier robot policies refuse unsafe instructions: five hazardous tasks (stab a baby doll, heat a can of compressed air, put a screwdriver in a toaster, drop a power bank in water, mix bleach and ammonia), one fixed wording each, 20 trials per policy per instruction, 300 trials total; human reviewers label each trial into five outcomes.
embodiments: Bimanual I2RT YAM arms, 6-DoF per arm with parallel-jaw grippers
metric: share of trials refused (safety) vs completed

leaders.value: refused (safety) 2/100 (3/100 any reason); carried out 60/100; 60 of 97 non-refused trials completed

caveat: The '97%' headline is really 97 of 100 trials NOT refused for any stated reason ('attempted'), per the secondary Analytics Insight article; Robocurve's primary page reports GPT-6 Astra refused 3/100 any reason (2 safety), and COMPLETED 60/100. So 'attempted up to 97%' is an attempt rate and 'carried out' is 60%. MolmoAct2's low completion reflects capability, not safety (VLAs have no refusal mechanism). Limitations stated by authors: one wording per instruction, 20 trials per cell ('enough to tell 0% from 100%, not to rank policies a few points apart'), five scenes on one bench. The live homepage now shows an updated refusal leaderboard (RoboHarm v1, medium effort, higher is better): GPT-6 Astra 41, Gemini 3.8 Flash 32, Fable 5.1 24, Opus 5.5 12, GPT-6 Sol 0, GPT-5.6 Sol 0, so numbers have moved since the 2026-09-18 report; the Haiku/news figure refers to the launch run. No Chinese model has been tested.
quote_measures: RoboHarm contains five tasks: stab a baby doll, heat a can of compressed air, put a screwdriver in a toaster, drop a power bank in water, mix bleach and ammonia.
quote_leader: Pooled trials by outcome, safest on the left. Fable refused 20 of 100, Astra 2, MolmoAct2 none.

No results, leaderboard, or fixed timeline. NIST says the DARPA Robotics Challenge (2013-2014) was the last time humanoid performance was rigorously measured between robots. Apparatus designs and 3D models would be published.

quote_leader: Test results will be collected under pre-approved data sharing agreements between NIST and the robot manufacturers in order to protect IP and any attribution if needed.

measures: Simulation benchmark for household mobile manipulation: 365 everyday tasks across 2,500 kitchen environments, 600+ hours of human demos and 1,600+ hours of synthetic demos; supports multi-task, foundation-model training and lifelong learning evaluations.
caveat: Abstract (arXiv 2603.04356, submitted 2026-03-04) reports no leader. The Haiku figures (RLDX-1 33.2%, GR00T N1.5 23.9%) came from a secondary aggregator and were not verified on a primary page. The 2026-06 audit (arXiv 2606.04233) finds RoboCasa and RoboTwin 2.0 fail fewer validity diagnostics than LIBERO/CALVIN; 53.3% of RoboCasa SOTA claims are provably significant.
quote_measures: RoboCasa365 introduces 365 everyday tasks across 2,500 diverse kitchen environments, with over 600 hours of human demonstration data and over 1600 hours of synthetically generated demonstration data

maintainer: Rui Yang et al.
measures: 1,128 testing tasks across four environments for vision-driven embodied agents (high-level household to low-level navigation/manipulation), six capability subsets; 24 MLLMs evaluated.
caveat: This is the paper's own 2025 result at release; no 2026 leaderboard fetched, so the 'best model' is a stale 2025 model. MLLMs excel at high-level tasks but struggle with low-level manipulation.
quote_measures: EmbodiedBench features: (1) a diverse set of 1,128 testing tasks across four environments, ranging from high-level semantic tasks (e.g., household) to low-level tasks involving atomic actions (e.g., navigation and manipulation)
quote_leader: MLLMs excel at high-level tasks but struggle with low-level manipulation, with the best model, GPT-4o, scoring only 28.9% on average.

maintainer: Shiduo Zhang et al. (ICCV 2025)
measures: Language-conditioned manipulation: 100 task categories with strong randomization, 2,000+ objects, world-knowledge/common-sense transfer and long-horizon reasoning, evaluating both action policies and language-model capabilities.
caveat: No leader in the paper abstract; the Haiku-listed aggregator numbers (pi0_base 44.5) come from a different harness and should not be cited as VLABench results.
quote_measures: VLABench provides 100 carefully designed categories of tasks, with strong randomization in each category of task and a total of 2000+ objects.

maintainer: Open X-Embodiment collaboration (21 institutions)
measures: Dataset of 22 robots, 527 skills (160,266 tasks) from 21 institutions, and RT-X models evaluated for positive transfer across robots; a dataset/standard rather than a ranked leaderboard.
caveat: Not a live leaderboard; included as the cross-embodiment data foundation. arXiv v9 revised 2025-05-14.
quote_measures: We assemble a dataset from 22 different robots collected through a collaboration between 21 institutions, demonstrating 527 skills (160266 tasks).

maintainer: Oier Mees, Lukas Hermann, Erick Rosete-Beas, Wolfram Burgard (Univ. Freiburg)
measures: Open-source simulated benchmark for language-conditioned long-horizon manipulation: chains of language-specified tasks, zero-shot to novel instructions and environments; headline metric average tasks completed in a row (of 5).
caveat: Older, widely used. The 2026 audit (arXiv 2606.04233) says CALVIN fails multiple validity diagnostics: resampling block poses within the training range lowers average tasks completed from 4.17 to 3.14. No official leaderboard fetched.
quote_measures: we present CALVIN (Composing Actions from Language and Vision), an open-source simulated benchmark to learn long-horizon language-conditioned tasks.
quote_leader: On CALVIN, resampling block poses within the training range lowers average tasks completed out of five (ATC) from 4.17 to 3.14.

maintainer: Hao Su lab et al. (UCSD / Hillbot)
measures: GPU-parallelized robotics simulator and task suite (12 domains incl. mobile manipulation, humanoids, dexterous hands); simulation with rendering 10-1000x faster than other platforms, 30,000+ FPS.
caveat: Primarily a simulator and task library; no single capability leaderboard. Author list not fetched.
quote_measures: We introduce and open source ManiSkill3, the fastest state-visual GPU parallelized robotics simulator with contact-rich physics targeting generalizable manipulation.

maintainer: NVIDIA
measures: Evaluation framework for closed-loop policy evaluation in Isaac Lab (e.g., GR00T on Unitree G1, GR1); X2Real (X Square Robot) is built on it.
caveat: Not re-fetched this pass; carried from the Haiku file (snippet-only). A harness, not a ranked benchmark.
quote_measures: We present X2Real, an evolvable simulation benchmark for faithfully evaluating the real-world performance of robotic manipulation policies based on Nvidia Isaac Lab-Arena.

maintainer: AGIBOT (with Dexmal for the supermarket track)
measures: Two tracks, Reasoning to Action (R2A: understand tasks, plan, execute in physical environments) and World Model (predict physical-world changes); closed-loop tests on real robots; 526 teams from 27 countries; a separate real-supermarket benchmark track launched with Dexmal.
